text:
Mireille Ashgrove has won this year's Calder Vane Prize for architecture, taking an award of 85,000 vane-marks from a field of 212 submitted projects.

The announcement came on 14 March at the Calder Vane Foundation's annual ceremony. Tobias Wrenfield, chair of the jury, presented the award and read the citation.

The jury singled out Ashgrove's Lowmere Harbour Pavilion. Its published citation, "Statement of the Calder Vane Architecture Jury," praised the project and formed the basis of the award.

By the numbers: roughly one entry in 212 takes the prize, a selectivity that keeps the award closely watched.

What it means for the sector: a Calder Vane win typically sharpens attention on the recipient's practice. Expect Ashgrove's profile, and interest in harbour-front and public-pavilion work more broadly, to rise in the months ahead.
